questions.q: Among the following, which is the strongest oxidizing agent?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The substance which will have the highest& value of reduction potential will be the strongest oxidising agent. The values of reduction potential are as follow

{E}_{{Mn}^{3 +} / {Mn}^{2 +}}^{0} = + 1 .57 V
{E}_{{Ti}^{3 +} / {Ti}^{2 +}}^{0} = - 0 .37 V
{E}_{{Fe}^{3 +} / {Fe}^{2 +}}^{0} = + 0 .77 V
{E}_{{Cr}^{3 +} / {Cr}^{2 +}}^{0} = - 0 .41 V

As we can see~${Mn}^{+ 3}$& has the highest& value of standard reduction potential, so& it will be the strongest oxidising agent.

The common oxidation state of lanthanide& is& $+ 3$. The lanthanide ions having~$+ 2$~oxidation state undergo oxidation readily, hence they act as reducing agents.~The lanthanide ions having~ $+ 4$oxidation state undergo reduction~readily, hence they act as oxidising~agents.

questions.q: Consider the hydrated ions of $Ti^{2 +}, V^{2 +}, Ti^{3 +}$ and $Sc^{3 +}$ . The correct order of their spin-only magnetic moments is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$Magnetic moment \left(\mu\right) = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}$
More than value of n, more will be magnetic moment.
$Ti^{+ 2}$ electronic configuration;
$3d^{2}$ $\mu = \sqrt{2\left(2 + 2\right)} = 2.82$
${\text{Ti}}^{+ 3} ⇒ 3d^{1}$ $\mu = \sqrt{1\left(1 + 2\right)} = \sqrt{3} = 1.73$
$V^{+ 2} ⇒ 3d^{3}$ $\mu = \sqrt{3 \left(3 + 2\right)} = 3.87$
$Sc^{3 +} ⇒ \left[Ar\right]$ no unpaired electron. $\to \mu = 0$
Hence Order of Magnetic Moment is $V^{+ 2} > Ti^{+ 2} > Ti^{+ 3} > Sc^{+ 3}$

Chromate reacts rapidly with hydrogen peroxide to exchange two oxo ligands and become diperoxochromate(VI)

$\mathop{CrO42 -}_{yellowsolution}\to 3 . 10 % {H}_{2}{O}_{2}

Hence, the answer is option A.

questions.q: Which one of the following lanthanoids does not form ${MO}_{2}$? [$M$ is lanthanoid metal]

questions.solution:
$Yb$ is the only element that does not form ${MO}_{2}$ type oxide.

Ytterbium is a soft, malleable and rather ductile element that exhibits a bright silvery luster. questions.q: Prolonged heating is avoided during the preparation of ferrous ammonium sulphate to
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The formula for ferrous ammonium sulphate is ${FeSO}_{4} . ( {NH}_{4}{)}_{2}{SO}_{4} . 6{H}_{2}O$. It is prepared by dissolving equimolar mixture of hydrated ferrous sulphate and ammonium sulphate~in water containing a little sulphuric acid. The solution is subjected to crystallisation, ferrous ammonium sulphate separates out from the solution.

The chemical reaction is given below.

${FeSO}_{4} + ( {NH}_{4}{)}_{2}{SO}_{4} + 6{H}_{2}O \to {FeSO}_{4} . ( {NH}_{4}{)}_{2}{SO}_{4} . 6{H}_{2}O ( Mohr ’ ssalt )$

Avoid prolonged heating while preparing crystals of ferrous ammonium sulphate, as it may oxidise ferrous ions to ferric ions and change the stoichiometry of the crystals.

questions.q: Which one of the lanthanoids given below is the most stable in divalent form?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${Ce}^{+ 2}: \left(xe\right)4f^{2}$

${Eu}^{+ 2}: \left(xe\right)4f^{7}$

${Sm}^{+ 2}: \left(xe\right)4f^{6}$

${Yb}^{+ 2}: \left(xe\right)4f^{14}$

As~${Yb}^{+ 2}and{Eu}^{+ 2}$~has completely filled and half filled~$4f$~orbital, so they~would be the most stable. But among the these two~${Eu}^{+ 2}$~is more stable based on reduction potential value.

${E}_{M^{3 +} / M^{2 +}}^{°} ⇒ $\begin{cases}Eu & Yb \\ - 0 . 35 & - 1 . 05\end{cases}$$

Hence, due to more reduction potential in $Eu$ as compared to $Yb$, it can concluded that ${Eu}^{2 +}$ is more stable than ${Yb}^{2 +}$.

questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment value of the most basic oxide of vanadium among ${V}_{2}{O}_{3}$' ${V}_{2}{O}_{4}$ and ${V}_{2}{O}_{5}$ is____B.M. (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${V}_{2}{O}_{3}$~is the most basic oxide among the given oxides.

In~${V}_{2}{O}_{3}$, Vanadium is in~$+ 3$~oxidation state

$V^{3 +} ⇒ \left[Ar\right]3d^{2}4s^{0}$

So,~$2$~unpaired electrons are there,

Its magnetic moment is equal to~$\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}BM = \sqrt{2\left(2 + 2\right)}BM$

$= 2 . 83BM ≃ 3BM$

($n =$& number of unpaired electrons)

questions.q: In the reaction of potassium dichromate, potassium chloride and sulfuric acid (conc.), the oxidation state of the chromium in the product is  \left(+\right)$ _______.$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The oxidation state or oxidation number is defined as the loss or gain of electrons from an atom, molecule, or compound.

The reaction of potassium dichromate, potassium chloride and sulphuric acid (conc.)is as follows,

${K}_{2}{Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}\left(s\right) + 4KCl\left(s\right) + 6{H}_{2}{SO}_{4} ( conc . )$

$\to 2{CrO}_{2}{Cl}_{2}\left(g\right) + 6{KHSO}_{4} + 3{H}_{2}O$

This reaction takes place in chromyl chloride test.

The Chromyl chloride is a neutral molecule as it does not have any charge on it.

Here, oxidation state of $Cr$ in ${CrO}_{2}{Cl}_{2}$ is $+ 6$.

questions.q: The oxidation state of manganese in the product obtained in a reaction of potassium permanganate and hydrogen peroxide in basic medium is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
This ${KMnO}_{4}$~is a powerful oxidizing agent in neutral, acidic, and alkaline medium. The ${H}_{2}{O}_{2}$~is also an oxidizing agent but in the reaction of ${KMnO}_{4}$~with the ${H}_{2}{O}_{2}$. The ${H}_{2}{O}_{2}$loses its electron and acts as a reducing agent. In an acidic medium, the${MnO}_{4}^{-}$ ions involve the addition of 5 electrons and the two peroxide ions give out two electrons. In dilute alkaline medium or in neutral medium~${MnO}_{4}^{-}$~ions involve the addition of 3 electrons. The reaction in basic medium is given below.

$2{KMnO}_{4} + 3{H}_{2}{O}_{2}\overset{basicmedium}{⟶}\overset{+ 4}{2{MnO}_{2}} + 3{O}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O + 2KOH$

The oxidation state of~$Mn\text{in}{MnO}_{2}$~is~$+ 4 .$
